Accenture (NYSE: ACN) reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $18.04B, reaching the top of its guided range, and new bookings of $22.1B, up 6% in USD
Year-to-date performance through the first half of fiscal 2026 showed total revenues of $36.8 billion, up 4% in local currency and 7% in U.S. dollars. Adjusted earnings per share for the half reached $6.87, a 7% increase, excluding business optimization costs of $0.40 per share.

Cash generation remained robust, with free cash flow of $3.7 billion in the quarter and $5.2 billion year-to-date. The company returned $2.7 billion to shareholders during Q2 through $1.7 billion in accelerated share repurchases and $1.0 billion in dividends. Accenture increased its quarterly dividend by 10% to $1.63 per share, marking continued commitment to shareholder returns despite market headwinds.

## Forward-Looking Statements and Raised Guidance [...] ## Quarterly Performance Highlights

The company delivered revenues of $18.0 billion for the quarter, representing 8% growth in U.S. dollars and 4% in local currency, surpassing analyst forecasts of $17.83 billion. Earnings per share reached $2.93, beating expectations of $2.85 and marking a 4% year-over-year increase. Operating margin expanded 30 basis points to 13.8%, demonstrating improved operational efficiency.

The presentation highlighted several performance metrics across key business dimensions. Geographic performance showed divergent trends, with Asia Pacific leading at 10% local currency growth, followed by Americas at 3% and EMEA at 2%. From an industry perspective, Communications, Media & Technology led with 10% growth, while Health & Public Service declined 1%. [...] ## Forward-Looking Statements and Raised Guidance

Despite the challenging market environment, Accenture raised its full-year fiscal 2026 outlook. The company now expects revenue growth of 3% to 5% in local currency, or 4% to 6% excluding the impact of Accenture Federal Services (AFS). This represents an improvement from the prior range of 2% to 5% provided in December.

Adjusted earnings per share guidance was narrowed and raised to a range of $13.65 to $13.90, representing 6% to 8% growth over adjusted fiscal 2025 results. Perhaps most significantly, the company increased its free cash flow guidance by $1 billion to a range of $10.8 billion to $11.5 billion, suggesting confidence in working capital management and collections.
